additional_info.subject: ID0443875-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P9 170000901] Faulty Charging Cable CRM:02699000170
additional_info.body:
Hello Lital, good morning. I hope you are doing well.
I checked the CCS and we do not have temperature values:
As you can see the resistance = 0 ohm.
Since this is a LCC, we can only measure the CAN communication since this is the responsible for the readings:
First we need to measure 60Ohm between High and Low, by measuring between XD12:7B and 8D. We need to measure we measure in this 7B and 8D specifically to confirm if the defect is in the cable or the signal is lost somewhere until the KF11.
If we don't have 60Ohm, then the microcontroller is faulty and the cable needs to be replaced.
Second, if we have 60Ohm, then we must follow this 60Ohm until the input of KF11 CAN 1L and 1H.
If the signal is lost until there, we should check if there is any loose cable.
Third, if we have 60Ohm until KF11 and still it doesn't work, try these two options by order:
Replace the black connector with a spare one (the EcoG has some that are not used at all)
If it still doesn't work, please try replacing the KF11.
If it doesn't work, then we need to replace the CCS Cable
@Orel I will send this ticket to you, if you need any help just ping me.
Best regards,
Francisco

Hello
eMobility Tech Support Team,
We performed the measurements,
130 ohm's values ​​were measured at the points that were specified to us that should be below 60 ohm's.
In addition, we tried to replace the KF11 part, but the charger reset at 30% each time - meaning that it seems that the update was unsuccessful. (Possibly due to the difference between the versions)
We disassembled the replacement KF11 part from another charger with the serial number attached in the picture.
What are the next steps for testing to diagnose the fault?
Please advise.
Best Regards,
Doron Yavelberg
Maintenance Manager
AFCON ELECTRIC TRANSPORTATION LTD
